profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC17 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC17 sits in Ashburn, Virginia, in Data Center Alley, a region containing roughly 10 million square feet of data center space and described as the greatest concentration of data center capacity on the planet. The facility is part of Equinix's multi-building Ashburn campus, which has grown from the operator's original late-1990s DC1 and DC2 buildings into numbered facilities extending into the twenties. Equinix does not publish DC17's power capacity, square footage, or specific certifications.

The Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast and offers colocation, managed solutions, interconnection products, and metro connectivity. The operator has described representative campus buildings as offering N+1 power and cooling redundancy, 30-plus-hour generator endurance, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High, though these specifications are not confirmed for DC17 specifically. Cabinet densities on the campus are described as a minimum of 4 kilowatts per cabinet.

Across Virginia, 23 facilities have published megawatt figures totaling 1,375 megawatts, and DC17 is not among them. The campus rank by published capacity cannot be determined because Equinix has chosen not to disclose this building's power draw. Without published specifications, DC17 cannot be weighed against other facilities in the state or used to assess whether this site matters to AI scaling.
